title: Release Origami — warmup + pin protocol (sketch)
body:
Goal: sketch a lightweight, low-cognitive warmup and pin protocol that teams can use for small model flips or kernel upgrades. Keep operations mostly manual for first two folds, then automate the fold/unfold once signals are stable.

Context: since the last Dedicated->Hosted drift incident we want a tiny ritual that reduces blast radius when flipping model variants (quantized vs fp16, new tokenizer, runtime kernel swap). This is a personal crib to try against the edge release next quarter.

Metaphor: think of the rollout as origami — two basic fold types we use:
- valley-folds: quiet, incremental traffic absorption (slowly add users)
- mountain-folds: fast expansion when confident (double traffic quickly)
Leave visible crease markers (telemetry checkpoints) between folds.

Assumptions:
- Canary clients: 2–4 internal tenants with stable request patterns.
- Telemetry: p95 latency, request error rate (4xx/5xx), decoder token error spikes, hallucination proxy (where available), and cost-per-token approximation.
- Run during low global traffic hours if > 10% traffic change.

Warmup outline (high-level):
1) Prep (T-24h)
   - Pin model variant in config repo as "origami-v1" (decouple from deploy tag).
   - Add temporary route in traffic-router: /v-origami -> origami-v1, keep current live route unchanged.
   - Notify SRE + oncall slack channel: #releases (short blurb + roll window).
   - Smoke tests: perf/local accuracy against short evaluation set (5 prompts).

2) Fold 1 — valley (T0 -> +10m)
   - Move 0.5% of traffic from live -> origami via router config.
   - Duration: 10m observation.
   - Signals to watch: p95 latency delta < +40ms, errors < 0.15%, tail memory OOM none.
   - If any threshold breached: revert traffic immediately and capture trace links.

3) Fold 2 — valley (T+10m -> +1h)
   - Move to 2% traffic.
   - Run a small set of synthetic user journeys (background job) for 30m.
   - Monitor deploy dashboard + token-cost estimate.

4) Fold 3 — valley (T+1h -> +3h)
   - Move to 8% traffic.
   - Begin A/B quality checks (auto evals on small prompt corpus).

5) Mountain fold (manual gating)
   - If quality + perf stable for 3h, jump to 25% then 50% (each jump 20m apart) — only for low-risk kernel patches.
   - If anything weird: pin back to previous stable variant and hold.

Pinning semantics (notes):
- Two independent pins: runtime-pin (routing) and model-pin (config + audit). Both must be recorded.
- Runtime pin example: record pair <route,origami-v1> in release-notes and in pin-db (manual entry).
- Model-pin example: PR diff in config repo with comment prefix: "release-origami-pin: <date> <owner>".

Safety gates & thresholds (quick):
- p95 latency increase > +80ms for 10m -> rollback.
- 4xx/5xx increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute (not relative) for 10m -> rollback.
- Token hallucination proxy score jump > 30% -> hold and run deeper quality evals.
- Memory OOM seen on any host -> immediate rollback and forensic capture.

Telemetry checks (what to watch in first 3 folds):
- Per-route token consumption slope (abnormal increases could indicate runaway generation).
- Per-client error aggregation (some tenants pulse differently).
- Cold start latency for first requests after scale-up (important for Dedicated).
- KV-cache miss ratio (new kernels might flush differently).

Quick operational cmds (handy)
- route traffic: curl -XPOST "https://router.internal/api/route" -d '{"from":"live","to":"origami-v1","pct":0.5}'
- sample logs: ssh ops@log-collector 'jq .message | grep origami-v1 | tail -n 200'
- pin in DB: psql -c "INSERT INTO release_pins (tag,owner,reason) VALUES ('origami-v1','lee','warmup flip')"
(These are notes — real automation uses infra PRs and router UI)

Nightwatch checklist (handheld for oncall)
- 00: confirm smoke tests green pre-fold
- 10: check p95 & errors, check SLI dashboard link, post short update in slack
- 30: snapshot a sample of prompt/responses for human spot check (link to gist)
- 60: decide whether to continue valley or hold

Open questions / TODO (personal):
- Should we add a small synthetic traffic generator that mimics LLM token patterns? (Tomás likes it)
- How to better instrument hallucination proxy cheaply? Current eval infra is heavy.
- Can we store pin metadata in a single place (git + database + console) to avoid mismatches? (one-writer policy?)
- Add a one-click revert button in the router UI that both flips routing and creates a rollback PR.

Postmortem capture template (one-liners):
- What changed: <model variant / kernel>
- When did we fold/unfold: <timestamps>
- Observed signal delta: p95 +Xms, errors +Y%
- Root cause hypothesis: <human></human>
- Next action items: small list

Personal notes: keep this intentionally lean — 3 folds + optional mountain jump. Test it in staging three times before I propose automation. If Anika + Tomás both say green twice, escalate to infra for router API hook.

---
End of sketch. If I run this, will try origami-v1 on regional subset first (us-west only) and leave EU out for first two weeks.
summary: Personal draft: a small ritualized warmup and pin protocol using an "origami" metaphor. Valley folds for slow absorption, mountain fold for confident jumps. Manual gating, explicit pins in config + DB, short telemetry thresholds and checklist. Open questions about synthetic traffic and unified pin storage.
